sentences.en: Okay, so we have a question here from Joshua D.
sentences.zh: 好的，这里有一个来自约书亚·D·

sentences.en: Terry.
sentences.zh: 特里（Joshua D. Terry）的问题。

sentences.en: To what extent was Alexander's conquest of Persia actually intended as revenge for campaigns of Darius I and Xerxes in the 5th century BC?
sentences.zh: 亚历山大对波斯的征服，在多大程度上实际上是为了报复公元前5世纪大流士一世和薛西斯的远征？

sentences.en: So those are the kings.
sentences.zh: 所以这些就是那些国王。

sentences.en: Darius sends expedition to Marathon.
sentences.zh: 大流士派远征军去马拉松。

sentences.en: Xerxes led the great expedition that ends up burning Athens in 480 BC.
sentences.zh: 薛西斯领导的那次伟大的远征，最终在公元前480年烧毁了雅典。

sentences.en: We mentioned in the previous episode that Philip has been using this as a kind of justification to get the Greeks on board.
sentences.zh: 我们在上一集中提到过，腓力一直以此作为把希腊人拉拢到自己阵营的某种借口。

sentences.en: Alexander turns up in Persepolis.
sentences.zh: 亚历山大出现在波斯波利斯。

sentences.en: Persepolis, of all the great Persian capitals, is the one that's most associated with the Achaemenid dynasty, the dynasty of Persian kings to which Darius III belongs.
sentences.zh: 在所有伟大的波斯首都中，波斯波利斯是与阿契美尼德王朝联系最紧密的城市，也就是大流士三世所属的那个波斯国王王朝。

sentences.en: In Babylon and in Susa, Alexander has behaved with exemplary forbearance.
sentences.zh: 在巴比伦和苏萨，亚历山大表现出了堪称典范的宽容。

sentences.en: Perbearance.
sentences.zh: 克制。

sentences.en: In fact, at Susa, he allows the Persian commander of the citadel there to stay in office.
sentences.zh: 事实上，在苏萨，他允许那里的城堡波斯指挥官继续留任。

sentences.en: So he's already accommodating himself to the local elites when he's...
sentences.zh: 所以当他……的时候，他已经在适应当地精英了。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是这样。

sentences.en: And in due course, he's going to appoint, I think, a Persian as satrap of Babylon.
sentences.zh: 而且在适当的时候，我想他会任命一个波斯人担任巴比伦的总督。

sentences.en: So essentially, he's already, you know, he's a great general, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 所以本质上，你知道的，他已经是个伟大的将领了，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, he's top general.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他是顶级将领。

sentences.en: But he's also a brilliant, brilliant political strategiSt.
sentences.zh: 但他同时也是一位极其出色的政治战略家。

sentences.en: He clearly has this astonishing ability to read a situation politically as well as militarily.
sentences.zh: 他显然具备这种令人惊叹的能力，能在政治上和军事上同时看清局势。

sentences.en: And he understands, in a way that many, many of the Macedonians don't, that the only way
sentences.zh: 他以许多马其顿人所不具备的方式明白，唯一的途径

sentences.en: that he can possibly hope to establish Macedonian rule over this vast empire that he's conquered is, in a sense, to get the Persians on board.
sentences.zh: ——即他有可能希望在这个自己征服的庞大帝国上建立马其顿统治的唯一途径——在某种程度上，就是把波斯人拉拢过来。

sentences.en: I think that's absolutely right, Tom.
sentences.zh: 我想完全正确，汤姆。

sentences.en: Step into the platform heels of the great king himself.
sentences.zh: 踩上伟大大王本人的厚底高跟鞋。

sentences.en: I think he's more imaginative than some of his comrades.
sentences.zh: 我认为他比他的一些同僚更有想象力。

sentences.en: Vastly more imaginative.
sentences.zh: 何止更有想象力。

sentences.en: I mean, he's one of the most imaginative rulers who's ever lived, I would say.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我要说他是历史上最有想象力的统治者之一。

sentences.en: So he sees straight away, I think, when he gets there, this isn't now just a matter of, like, making ourselves very rich, going back and buying a big farm in Macedonia.
sentences.zh: 所以他一到那里就立刻看出，这现在不仅仅是像我们要变得非常富有、然后回去在马其顿买个大农场那样的事情了。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不。

sentences.en: This is, he suddenly thinks, the machine is ripe for the taking.
sentences.zh: 他突然觉得，这台机器已经成熟，唾手可得。

sentences.en: I can, I don't need to smash up the machine.
sentences.zh: 我可以，我不需要砸碎这台机器。

sentences.en: You decapitate it and you take it over.
sentences.zh: 你斩断它的首脑，然后接管它。

sentences.en: Yeah, I'll take it over.
sentences.zh: 对，我会接管它。

sentences.en: I'll do, you know, I'll take it over and get it to work for me.
sentences.zh: 我会，你知道的，我会接管它并让它为我工作。

sentences.en: I can be the next Persian king.
sentences.zh: 我可以成为下一个波斯国王。

sentences.en: I think that's basically what he thinks.
sentences.zh: 我想这基本上就是他的想法。

sentences.en: And why wouldn't you be?
sentences.zh: 而且你为什么不这么做呢？

sentences.en: It's a much better thing to be, as we've talked about in our Persian episode, it's a much better thing to be the leader of Persia than the leader of Macedonia.
sentences.zh: 就像我们在波斯那一集里讨论过的，成为波斯的领袖比成为马其顿的领袖要好得多。

sentences.en: But ideally, it'd be both.
sentences.zh: 但理想情况下，最好两者兼得。

sentences.en: Well, exactly, he can be both.
sentences.zh: 嗯，没错，他可以两者兼得。

sentences.en: That's what he's thinking.
sentences.zh: 这就是他的想法。

sentences.en: He thinks he can be ruler of everything.
sentences.zh: 他认为自己可以成为一切事物的统治者。

sentences.en: And pharaoh of Egypt.
sentences.zh: 还有埃及法老。

sentences.en: And he can, of course he is.
sentences.zh: 他可以，他当然是。

sentences.en: And he's king of the world in Babylon.
sentences.zh: 他还是巴比伦的世界之王。

sentences.en: I mean, he takes over all these titles.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他接管了所有这些头衔。

sentences.en: Well, they're interesting, he never actually takes over the title of king of kings.
sentences.zh: 嗯，有趣的是，他实际上从未接管过“万王之王”的头衔。

sentences.en: So that's a step too far.
sentences.zh: 所以那是走得太远了。

sentences.en: A step too far, but he does take over the kind of the regional ones.
sentences.zh: 走得太远了，但他确实接管了诸如地区之王之类的头衔。

sentences.en: And so he, you know, so he treats Babylon and Susa as a Persian king would treat Babylon and Susa.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，他对待巴比伦和苏萨的方式就像一个波斯国王对待巴比伦和苏萨的方式一样。

sentences.en: Yeah, but then Persepolis.
sentences.zh: 对，但接下来的就是波斯波利斯了。

sentences.en: Persepolis is different because Persepolis is...
sentences.zh: 波斯波利斯不同，因为波斯波利斯是……

sentences.en: The dynastic capital of the Echaemenids.
sentences.zh: 阿契美尼德王朝的都城。

sentences.en: So what's he going to do with it?
sentences.zh: 那他要怎么对它呢？

sentences.en: And he, basically, he ends up deciding he's going to burn it.
sentences.zh: 基本上，他最终决定把它烧毁。

sentences.en: Well, this is the question.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这就是问题所在。

sentences.en: Because some sources, the great story is that they're having a great sort of drinking about one night.
sentences.zh: 因为根据一些资料，最著名的故事是他们有一天晚上在痛饮狂欢。

sentences.en: And so this is what ties in with Joshua Terry's question about, is it revenge for the burning Athens?
sentences.zh: 这与约书亚·特里的问题联系在了一起：这究竟是不是为了报复烧毁雅典？

sentences.en: So some people say he does this as policy.
sentences.zh: 所以有些人说他是出于政策需要而这么做的。

sentences.en: He always meant to do it.
sentences.zh: 他一直都打算这么做。

sentences.en: And he deliberately said, I'm going to burn down this fantastic columned hall and all these wooden ceilings and stuff as revenge.
sentences.zh: 他故意说，我要把这座美妙的圆柱大厅和所有这些木制天花板之类的东西烧掉作为报复。

sentences.en: Deliberate revenge for the destruction of the temples.
sentences.zh: 蓄意报复对神庙的破坏。

sentences.en: But then other sources say, no, they're having a great evening.
sentences.zh: 但其他资料却说，不，他们当时正过得很愉快。

sentences.en: And this is the first point at which you realize that they've actually not come without female company.
sentences.zh: 这是你第一次意识到他们其实并不是孤身前来、没有女性陪伴的。

sentences.en: They've brought all their girlfriends with them and courtesans.
sentences.zh: 他们把所有的女朋友和交际花都带来了。

sentences.en: Athenian prostitutes.
sentences.zh: 雅典妓女。

sentences.en: Athenian prostitutes.
sentences.zh: 雅典妓女。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.zh: 所以托勒密有个最喜欢的宠姬叫什么来着？

sentences.en: Tais.
sentences.zh: 塔伊斯（Thais）。

sentences.en: Is something like that?
sentences.zh: 是不是类似这样的名字？

sentences.en: I don't know how you would pronounce it.
sentences.zh: 我不知道该怎么发音。

sentences.en: And she says, they're all absolutely hammered.
sentences.zh: 她说，他们当时都喝得酩酊大醉。

sentences.en: And she says-
sentences.zh: 然后她说——

sentences.en: She's Athenian.
sentences.zh: 她是雅典人。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: She's Athenian.
sentences.zh: 她是雅典人。

sentences.en: She says, you know, you've done a really good job, Alexander, but why don't you let me lead us in burning down Persepolis?
sentences.zh: 她说，你知道的，亚历山大，你干得真棒，但你为什么不让我带头把波斯波利斯烧掉呢？

sentences.en: And he says, ah, great idea.
sentences.zh: 他说，啊，好主意。

sentences.en: And so they all get torches and they burn it down.
sentences.zh: 于是他们都拿着火把把它给烧了。

sentences.en: And historians have argued ever since, is this, did she really do this?
sentences.zh: 从那以后，历史学家们一直在争论：这事真的是她干的吗？

sentences.en: I think not.
sentences.zh: 我觉得没有。

sentences.en: You don't think so?
sentences.zh: 你觉得不是？

sentences.en: No, I don't.
sentences.zh: 不，我不这么认为。

sentences.en: I think she did.
sentences.zh: 我觉得就是她干的。

sentences.en: That's a great story.
sentences.zh: 这是一个绝佳的故事。

sentences.en: It is a great story.
sentences.zh: 确实是个绝佳的故事。

sentences.en: And it's, and the thing about Alexander is he attracts great stories.
sentences.zh: 而且关于亚历山大的一点是，他总能吸引各种精彩的故事。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Like blotting paper soaks up ink.
sentences.zh: 就像吸墨纸吸收墨水一样。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: He, clearly he burns down Persepolis.
sentences.zh: 他显然烧毁了波斯波利斯。

sentences.en: But the question is, why does he do it?
sentences.zh: 但问题是，他为什么要这么做？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And the interesting thing though, Tom, is when you read the academic historians, they divide pretty much 50-50 on all the big questions.
sentences.zh: 不过有趣的是，汤姆，当你阅读学院派历史学家的著作时，他们对所有重大问题的看法几乎是对半开的。

sentences.en: And it's clearly because some can't bring themselves to let go of the story they read when they were about nine.
sentences.zh: 这显然是因为有些人无法割舍他们在大约九岁时读到的那个故事。

sentences.en: Well, I, I mean, you know, we don't know.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我，我的意思是，你知道的，我们并不知道。

sentences.en: We don't know.
sentences.zh: 我们不知道。

sentences.en: I mean, you know, you've got to toss a coin.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你知道的，你得抛硬币决定了。

sentences.en: You could say that he did it.
sentences.zh: 你可以说他是这么做的。

sentences.en: And clearly, I would suspect, and this depends on rating Alexander, but I would rate Alexander's political intelligence.
sentences.zh: 显然，我猜想——这取决于对亚历山大的评价——但我会赞赏亚历山大的政治智慧。

sentences.en: Obviously, Burning Down Persepolis is going to play well with the Greeks back home.
sentences.zh: 很明显，烧毁波斯波利斯会在国内的希腊人中间产生很好的反响。

sentences.en: And Alexander is always looking back to Greece.
sentences.zh: 而亚历山大总是心系希腊。

sentences.en: There's been kind of stirrings.
sentences.zh: 当时已经有一些骚动了。

sentences.en: There's been kind of, you know, the Spartans are still playing awkward.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，斯巴达人依然在找麻烦。

sentences.en: The Athenians are restive.
sentences.zh: 雅典人也躁动不安。

sentences.en: At some point, Alexander is going to send the Greeks back home.
sentences.zh: 在某个时刻，亚历山大要将希腊人送回老家。

sentences.en: He's going to, so he needs to keep the Greeks on board.
sentences.zh: 他打算这么做，所以他需要把希腊人拉拢在自己这一边。

sentences.en: So Burning Down Persepolis, he can pitch that as being revenge for Athens.
sentences.zh: 因此烧毁波斯波利斯，他可以把它宣传为对雅典的报复。

sentences.en: Deep down, I think that probably makes sense.
sentences.zh: 从内心深处来看，我认为这可能说得通。

sentences.en: And I think it's also telling Persepolis is not the biggest city.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为这也说明了波斯波利斯并非最大的城市。

sentences.zh: 最大的城市是巴比伦。

sentences.en: And he doesn't hit the biggest city.
sentences.zh: 而他没有对最大的城市下手。

sentences.en: Well, why would you?
sentences.zh: 嗯，你为什么又要动手呢？

sentences.en: You need it.
sentences.zh: 你需要它。

sentences.en: Yeah, of course.
sentences.zh: 对，当然。

sentences.en: Persepolis is expendable.
sentences.zh: 波斯波利斯是可有可无的。

sentences.en: It's a great, you know, you can burn that down.
sentences.zh: 这是一个伟大的，你知道的，你可以把它烧掉。

sentences.en: It's a great political message, but you're not really losing that much.
sentences.zh: 这是一个极好的政治信号，但你其实并没有失去太多东西。

sentences.en: But also, you're not, also, you can frame it to the Persians that you're attacking the dynasty.
sentences.zh: 而且，你还可以向波斯人解释说你攻击的是那个王朝。

sentences.en: Yeah, not the, but not Persia itself.
sentences.zh: 对，而不是针对波斯本身。

sentences.en: Not Persia itself.
sentences.zh: 不是波斯本身。

sentences.en: Because you're, you're showing respect to Susa.
sentences.zh: 因为你对苏萨表现出了尊重。

sentences.en: And from this point on, having burnt down Persepolis, Alexander is going to go to great pains to show his respect for, for Persian custoMs.
sentences.zh: 从这一点开始，在烧毁了波斯波利斯之后，亚历山大将不遗余力地表现出他对波斯习俗的尊重。

sentences.en: But what he does next, Tom, is interesting because he doesn't say, I'm going to now stay and rule.
sentences.zh: 但汤姆，他接下来做的事很有趣，因为他并没有说“我现在要留下来统治”。

sentences.en: He says, Darius is still out there somewhere.
sentences.zh: 他说，大流士现在还在外面的某个地方。

sentences.en: He's fled with Bessus.
sentences.zh: 他跟贝苏斯一起逃走了。

sentences.en: We don't know where.
sentences.zh: 我们不知道在哪里。

sentences.en: Let's go after him.
sentences.zh: 我们去追他吧。

sentences.en: And so they all go after him.
sentences.zh: 于是他们都去追他了。

sentences.en: They do.
sentences.zh: 他们确实去了。

sentences.en: And by this point, Bessus has decided that he wants to be king.
sentences.zh: 到这个时候，贝苏斯已经决定自己想当国王了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: And so he takes over, calls himself Artaxas, he's the third, fourth, sorry.
sentences.zh: 于是他接管了权位，自称为阿塔克萨斯，他是第三个，第四个，抱歉。

sentences.en: And Alexander finds Darius bleeding to death, doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 然后亚历山大发现大流士流血过多而死，对吧？

sentences.en: He's been kind of abandoned.
sentences.zh: 他有点被抛弃了。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: They find, they, so the, the, the, he's been chained in a litter, uh, sort of, they're, they're charging across on the road, the great highway that leads to Khorasan in the eaSt.
sentences.zh: 他们发现，他们，所以那个，那个，他被锁在一个轿子里，呃，某种程度上，他们，他们沿着大路冲过去，通往东方呼罗珊的大道。

sentences.en: Um, they know that Darius is ahead of them and they stop one day and they see this sort of battered old litter or chariot or cart or something by a well.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他们知道大流士在他们前面，有一天他们停下来，在水井旁看到了这种破旧的旧轿子或战车或手推车之类的东西。

sentences.en: And they go and look and inside is Darius bleeding to death.
sentences.zh: 然后他们过去一看，里面是大流士，正流血过多而死。

sentences.en: And he says, uh, to the guy who finds him, who's called Polystratus, he says, tell
sentences.zh: 他对找到他的人说，呃，那个人叫波利斯特拉图斯，他说，告诉

sentences.en: And then he dies.
sentences.zh: 然后他就死了。

sentences.zh: 当然，还有另一个故事，绝对是真实发生过的。

sentences.en: Because the genius of this is that Alexander can now cast himself, um, as the avenger of Darius III, which then enables him to cast himself, you know, having burnt down Persepolis,
sentences.zh: 因为这其中的巧妙之处在于，亚历山大现在可以把自己塑造成，嗯，三世大流士的复仇者，这反过来又使他能够塑造自己，你知道的，在烧毁波斯波利斯之后，

sentences.zh: 他现在可以说，我是阿契美尼德王朝的继承人。

sentences.en: In the space of about five minutes, Alexander goes from, we must hurry, we must catch Darius and kill him.

sentences.zh: 现在这是另一点，汤姆。

sentences.zh: 他是长角的那个，还是说他在《古兰经》里吗？

sentences.en: He's the Dulkanein, the two-horned one, which can only be the horns of Amun.
sentences.zh: 他是祖卡尔奈因，双角者，这只能是阿蒙神的角。

sentences.en: So there's the amazing thing that the details of this, you know, this trip to Siwa where he goes to the oracle of Amun has this kind of distorted echo in the Koran,
sentences.zh: 所以令人惊奇的是，这些细节，你知道的，他去锡瓦拜访阿蒙神谕所的这次行程，在《古兰经》中有了一种扭曲的回声，

sentences.en: which is the kind of, you know, so opposed to idolatry and paganism and all that kind of stuff.
sentences.zh: 而《古兰经》本来是那种，你知道的，极力反对偶像崇拜、异教风气以及所有这类东西的。

sentences.en: And there he is.
sentences.zh: 而他就在那里。

sentences.en: And Alexander in the Koran, he's, you know, it's his pothos.
sentences.zh: 亚历山大在《古兰经》里，你知道的，这就是他的渴望（pothos）。

sentences.en: He's going to the limits of the earth.
sentences.zh: 他正走向大地的尽头。

sentences.en: But let's talk about limits.
sentences.zh: 但我们来谈谈极限吧。

sentences.en: We've got lots of questions from the listeners about legacy and empire and so on.
sentences.zh: 我们收到了听众关于遗产、帝国等等的大量问题。

sentences.en: So Jonathan Wilde has a question.
sentences.zh: 所以乔纳森·维尔德有一个问题。

sentences.en: Was his empire too big to last?
sentences.zh: 他的帝国太大了而无法持久吗？

sentences.en: Because obviously on his deathbed, according to the sources, which Tom believes are all made up, he famously says, they say, to whom will you leave your kingdom?
sentences.zh: 因为很显然，根据史料记载，在他临终时——汤姆认为这些记载都是编造的——他有一句名言，据说，别人问他：你把王国留给谁？

sentences.en: And Perdiccas, his regent, says to him, who ends up basically being his successor in some ways, says to him, who are you going to leave your kingdom to?
sentences.zh: 他的摄政佩尔狄卡斯对他说——在某种程度上他最终成为了继承人——对他说：你打算把王国留给谁？

sentences.en: And he says, toi cratistoi, to the strongeSt.
sentences.zh: 他说，致最强者（toi cratistoi）。

sentences.en: And then it all falls apart.
sentences.zh: 然后这一切就瓦解了。

sentences.en: The sort of the lads who've come with him all turn on one another and they all fight and kill each other.
sentences.zh: 那些跟着他来的小伙子们全都反目成仇，互相打斗、残杀。

sentences.en: And it ends up with Seleucus is the guy who basically takes over Persia and much of Asia.
sentences.zh: 最终塞琉古成为了接管波斯和亚洲大部分地区的人。

sentences.en: Ptolemy, Egypt, one of his generals, Antipater, and his son, Cassander, take Macedonia, don't they?
sentences.zh: 托勒密占领了埃及，他的一个将军，安提帕特和他的儿子卡山德占领了马其顿，对吧？

sentences.en: I'm not sure I've missed somebody out.
sentences.zh: 我不确定我是不是漏掉了什么人。

sentences.en: Well, you've got Antigonus.
sentences.zh: 嗯，还有安提柯。

sentences.en: Antigonus, that's right.
sentences.zh: 安提柯，没错。

sentences.en: Antigonus.
sentences.zh: 安提柯。

sentences.en: Antigonus is the one eye.
sentences.zh: 独眼安提柯。

sentences.en: He takes Asia Minor, is that right?
sentences.zh: 他占领了小亚细亚，是这样吗？

sentences.en: No, he initially rules the kind of the Persian stretch, the eastern stretch.
sentences.zh: 不，他最初统治的是波斯那一带，东部的那一片。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And then Seleucus takes over from him.
sentences.zh: 然后塞琉古接替了他。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: So it's a very Game of Thrones style scenario, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 所以这非常像是《权力的游戏》式的剧情，对吧？

sentences.en: The question is, could it have lasted?
sentences.zh: 问题是，它本能持久吗？

sentences.en: Tom, do you think it could have lasted?
sentences.zh: 汤姆，你觉得它本能持久吗？

sentences.en: I think if Alexander had lived, I think if he'd established a secure succession, I think it's perfectly possible.
sentences.zh: 我认为如果亚历山大活下来，如果他确立了稳固的继承顺序，我认为这完全是可能的。

sentences.en: Not too large.
sentences.zh: 并没有太大。

sentences.en: He would have had to make the center of gravity in Persia.
sentences.zh: 他本必须把重心放在波斯。

sentences.en: And the thing is, is that none of his successors, none of the Macedonian lads want to do that.
sentences.zh: 问题是，他的所有继承人，所有的马其顿小伙子们都不想这么做。

sentences.en: So the capital of the Seleucid Empire ends up Antioch, which is on the Mediterranean coaSt.
sentences.zh: 所以塞琉古帝国的首都最终落在了安条克，它在地中海沿岸。

sentences.en: Actually, it's not Syria now, is it?
sentences.zh: 其实现在它不属于叙利亚了吧？

sentences.en: I think it's this kind of weird chunk of Turkey, but it's basically in Syria.
sentences.zh: 我觉得它是土耳其那块奇怪的领土，但它基本上在叙利亚境内。

sentences.en: It's Antakya in Turkey.
sentences.zh: 那是土耳其的安塔基亚。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Egypt, of course, is Mediterranean.
sentences.zh: 埃及当然在地中海。

sentences.en: Macedonia is Mediterranean.
sentences.zh: 马其顿在地中海。

sentences.en: They don't want to be out eaSt.
sentences.zh: 他们不想留在东方。

sentences.en: Alexander did.
sentences.zh: 但亚历山大想。

sentences.en: And had Alexander ruled from Susa or Babylon or whatever, then, you know, with his prestige, with his political nous, I think he could have done it.
sentences.zh: 如果亚历山大从苏萨、巴比伦或别的地方进行统治，那么凭借他的威望、他的政治敏锐度，我认为他本可以做到这一点。

sentences.en: But he surely would have faced revolts in Greece and so on, wouldn't he?
sentences.zh: 但他肯定会面对希腊等地的叛乱，不是吗？

sentences.en: I mean, well, he might have done, but he might, but, but, but, you know, but he might have kind of ended up, well, you know, I'll cut Greece free.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，好吧，他可能会遇到，但他可能，但，但，但，你知道的，但他最终可能会变成，好吧，你知道的，我把希腊解放算了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: You know, he's, but also, I mean, he's got a massive, you know, he's got a big force in Macedonia.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他，而且同时，我的意思是，他有一支庞大的，你知道的，他在马其顿有一支庞大的军队。

sentences.en: I think that the infrastructure of Achaemenid rule is there and Alexander understands its value, which is why Pierre Brion calls him the last of the Achaemenids.
sentences.zh: 我认为阿契美尼德统治的基础设施是存在的，而亚历山大理解它的价值，这就是皮埃尔·布里安称他为“最后一个阿契美尼德人”的原因。

sentences.en: He, he, he, he could have been, you know, it could have kind of ended up that the Achaemenids go and Alexander's dynasty basically takes its place.
sentences.zh: 他，他，他，他本可以，你知道的，结果可能会是阿契美尼德王朝离去，而亚历山大的王朝基本上取而代之。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Rather like Egyptian, the way that Egyptian.
sentences.zh: 有点像埃及的，埃及那种方式。

sentences.en: A bit like Egyptians.
sentences.zh: 有点像埃及人。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: A bit like the Ptolemies in, in Egypt.
sentences.zh: 有点像埃及的托勒密王朝。

sentences.en: But the problem you have with that is that Alexander in all his lifetime has never really shown any interest, particularly.
sentences.zh: 但你所面临的问题是，亚历山大在他的一生中，从未真正表现出任何特别的兴趣。

sentences.en: I know he's shown great strategic and political nous in dealing with elites and so on, but he hasn't particularly shown an interest in just governing.
sentences.zh: 我知道他在应对精英阶层等方面表现出了极大的战略和政治敏锐度，但他并没有特别表现出对单纯治理国家的兴趣。

sentences.en: He's shown a lot of interest in fighting.
sentences.zh: 他对打仗表现出了极大的兴趣。

sentences.en: Again, I'm not sure that's true.
sentences.zh: 再说一次，我不确定这是真的。

sentences.en: I think he does.
sentences.zh: 我认为他有。

sentences.en: I think he, you know, his, his appointments of, of satraps, his, um, his concern with, um, military organization, with administrative organization.
sentences.zh: 我认为他，你知道的，他，他对总督的任命，他，嗯，他对军事组织、行政组织的关注。

sentences.en: I think it's, but don't you think it's telling that in the last year of his life, he's already thinking about a new expedition.
sentences.zh: 我认为这——难道你不觉得能说明问题的是，在他生命的最后一年，他已经在考虑一次新的远征了吗？

sentences.en: I mean, just take a break, mate, you know, settle down, found a dynasty.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，歇一会儿吧，老兄，你知道的，安定下来，创立一个王朝。

sentences.en: Do you need to go to Arabia?
sentences.zh: 你非要去阿拉伯不可吗？

sentences.en: That's what I would see as the.
sentences.zh: 这就是我所认为的……

sentences.en: Again.
sentences.zh: 又来了。

sentences.en: You're going to say you don't, you don't, you don't believe any of it happens.
sentences.zh: 你会说你，你，你不相信这一切发生过。

sentences.en: It was all a dream.
sentences.zh: 这一切都是一场梦。

sentences.en: We don't, we don't know.
sentences.zh: 我们不知道，我们真的不知道。

sentences.en: So, okay, let's, um, uh, what about the, so Jerry and many others, says Sam, our backroom, um, mogul.
sentences.zh: 所以，好吧，那我们，嗯，呃，杰瑞和许多其他人怎么说呢，萨姆说，我们幕后的，嗯，大佬。

sentences.en: Sam says, they've all asked, where is his body?
sentences.zh: 萨姆说，他们都问过，他的尸体在哪里？

sentences.en: Well, we know where his body kind of ended up, don't we?
sentences.zh: 好吧，我们知道他的尸体最后大概在哪里，对吧？

sentences.en: It ended up in Alexandria.
sentences.zh: 它最后到了亚历山大港。

sentences.en: Alexandria, where it gets visited by the future Emperor Augustus, who knocks off the tip of his nose.
sentences.zh: 亚历山大港，后来的屋大维皇帝曾去那里参拜，还打碎了亚历山大大帝的鼻尖。

sentences.en: Supposedly.
sentences.zh: 据说如此。

sentences.en: Now, I don't believe that story, actually.
sentences.zh: 不过，其实我不相信这个故事。

sentences.en: I think that story is clearly invented.
sentences.zh: 我认为这个故事显然是编造的。

sentences.en: Well, you know the story, you know the brilliant story.
sentences.zh: 好吧，你知道这个故事，你知道这个精彩的故事。

sentences.en: You know the brilliant theory about where his body is?
sentences.zh: 你知道那个关于他的尸体在哪里的精彩理论吗？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不知道。

sentences.en: Which is, but, um.
sentences.zh: 就是，但是，嗯。

sentences.en: Don't tell me it's in Salisbury.
sentences.zh: 别告诉我尸体在索尔兹伯里。

sentences.en: No, it's in Venice.
sentences.zh: 不，在威尼斯。

sentences.en: Because the, the Venetians arrive in Alexandria looking for the body of St. Mark.
sentences.zh: 因为，威尼斯人来到亚历山大港寻找圣马可的遗体。

sentences.en: Great.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: Because it's San Marco.
sentences.zh: 因为那是圣马可教堂。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Mark's body is meant to be buried there.
sentences.zh: 马可的遗体本该埋在那里。

sentences.en: Um, and they go in and it's a time of chaos in Alexandria.
sentences.zh: 嗯，然后他们去了，当时亚历山大港正处于混乱时期。

sentences.en: And they look around and they, they find this body in a kind of great shrine.
sentences.zh: 他们四处寻找，然后，在一个宏伟的圣殿里发现了这具尸体。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And so they assume it's St. Mark's body and they remove it and they take it to Venice.
sentences.zh: 所以他们认为这就是圣马可的遗体，于是将其移走并带回了威尼斯。

sentences.en: And so Alexander's body is in San Marco.
sentences.zh: 因此，亚历山大的遗体就在圣马可教堂里。

sentences.en: Do you believe that?
sentences.zh: 你相信这个吗？

sentences.en: I was about to say, you don't believe all these sources, but you believe that.
sentences.zh: 我正想说，你对所有这些史料都不信，但你居然信这个。

sentences.en: It's such a good, it's such a great theory that I'd want to believe it.
sentences.zh: 这个理论太棒了，太伟大了，让我真想去相信它。

sentences.en: Now, there might be some people listening to this podcast who say, well,
sentences.zh: 现在，听这个播客的人中可能会有人说，好吧，

sentences.en: you've described somebody who fought a lot of battles and climbed rocks and behaved in sort of outlandish ways.
sentences.zh: 你描述的这个人打过很多仗，爬过山，行为举止甚至有些离经叛道。

sentences.en: But so what, you know, is it anything more than a children's, than the, is it anything more than basically the Lord of the Rings without the ring for adults?
sentences.zh: 但那又怎样呢，你知道，这不就是一部没有魔戒的、写给成年人看的《魔戒》吗，除此之外它还有别的意义吗？

sentences.en: And does Alexander matter, do you think?
sentences.zh: 你觉得亚历山大重要吗？

sentences.en: I mean, obviously he inaugurates what we call the Hellenistic age, the idea of this synthesis of East and WeSt.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，很显然，他开启了我们所说的希腊化时代，也就是东西方融合的理念。

sentences.en: And, but do you think that would have happened anyway, or do you think it took Alexander and his conquests to do it?
sentences.zh: 但是，你认为无论如何这都会发生，还是说这必须归功于亚历山大和他的征服？

sentences.en: Well, there's a famous saying by a German historian in the twenties, Karl Becker, who said, without Alexander the Great, no Islamic civilization.
sentences.zh: 嗯，二十年代有一位德国历史学家卡尔·贝克说过一句名言：没有亚历山大大帝，就没有伊斯兰文明。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And no Christianity, arguably.
sentences.zh: 可以说，也没有基督教。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So he creates, he creates, you know, the Koine, the common Greek language, but you could say that the culture becomes a kind of Koine.
sentences.zh: 所以他创造了，你知道的，通用希腊语，但你也可以说这种文化变成了一种通用语。

sentences.en: It's a melting pot in which Greek, Persian, Mesopotamian, Jewish influences all kind of mix and mingle.
sentences.zh: 这是一个大熔炉，希腊、波斯、美索不达米亚和犹太的影响都在其中交融汇聚。

sentences.en: And that is the Petri dish from which Christianity, rabbinical Judaism, Islam will emerge.
sentences.zh: 而这就是基督教、犹太教拉比传统和伊斯兰教孕育而生的培养皿。

sentences.en: And those are absolutely seismic developments.
sentences.zh: 这些绝对是具有震撼意义的发展。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So I think Alexander does matter.
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得亚历山大确实很重要。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: I think also he matters, doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 我觉得他也很重要，不是吗？

sentences.en: Because of the model that he presents to Pompey, to, we mentioned Augustus.
sentences.zh: 因为他为庞培，为——我们刚才提到了屋大维——提供了榜样。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: So we've got a question from, from Gary Hicks.
sentences.zh: 那么，我们有一个来自加里·希克斯的问题。

sentences.en: Was Alexander actually great?
sentences.zh: 亚历山大真的伟大吗？

sentences.en: And if so, for what?
sentences.zh: 如果是的话，体现在哪些方面？

sentences.en: And in comparison to whom?
sentences.zh: 又是和谁相比呢？

sentences.en: That takes us back to the, as you said, our very, very first podcast where we talked about that.
sentences.zh: 这把我们带回了，正如你所说，我们非常、非常第一期的播客，我们在那里讨论过这个。

sentences.en: Alexander, it's, again, it seems to be the Romans who call him the Great.
sentences.zh: 亚历山大，同样，似乎是罗马人称他为大帝。

sentences.en: The earliest reference to him as great is in a play by a Roman playwright called Plautus in the early second century BC.
sentences.zh: 最早称他为大帝的记载见于公元前二世纪初罗马剧作家普劳图斯的一部戏剧中。

sentences.en: And he, it seems to kind of derive from a desire to, you know, there are lots of Alexanders who were Macedonian kings.
sentences.zh: 这似乎源于一种愿望，你知道的，有很多叫亚历山大的马其顿国王。

sentences.en: So he's Alexander who's the great and the Romans have this, you know, the cognomen, which is a kind of like a descriptive word.
sentences.zh: 所以他是“伟大的”亚历山大，罗马人有这种称号，也就是一种描述性的词汇。

sentences.en: Um, so, so, so, so the great is like a kind of Roman cognomen.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以，“大帝”就像是一种罗马式的称号。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And this is Pompey the great who.
sentences.zh: 这就是庞培大帝……

sentences.en: Pompey Magnus kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 类似于“大庞培”那种。

sentences.en: Pompey Magnus.
sentences.zh: 大庞培。

sentences.en: He, he goes to the East and he conquers, you know, vast swathes of what had been Alexander's empire.
sentences.zh: 他，他去东方征服了，你知道的，曾经属于亚历山大帝国的广袤领土。

sentences.en: And he brings back Alexander's cloak and he sports it.
sentences.zh: 他把亚历山大的斗篷带了回来并穿在身上。

sentences.en: I'm sure it definitely was Alexander's cloak.
sentences.zh: 我确信那绝对是亚历山大的斗篷。

sentences.en: I'm sure it was.
sentences.zh: 我确信一定是。

sentences.en: It's only like 300 years too late.
sentences.zh: 只是晚了大概300年而已。

sentences.en: And he adopts Alexander's hairstyle, this kind of Elvis quiff.
sentences.zh: 他还模仿亚历山大的发型，那种类似猫王式的卷发。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Um, and so that then beds down the idea of greatness.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以这就奠定了“伟大”的概念。

sentences.en: And of course the Romans have an ambivalent relationship to that because.
sentences.zh: 当然，罗马人对这种概念有着矛盾的情结，因为……

sentences.en: Of their distrust of kings, right?
sentences.zh: 他们对君主心存戒备，对吧？

sentences.en: The distrust of kings.
sentences.zh: 对君主的戒备。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And, and the, the, actually the question, you know, Rome is meant to be an empire without limits, according to Virgil.
sentences.zh: 而且，事实上，按照维吉尔的说法，罗马本应是一个没有边界的帝国。

sentences.en: What does that mean?
sentences.zh: 那是什么意思？

sentences.en: And so that's why there's this fascination with a king, a conqueror who dreams of an empire without limits.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么人们会着迷于一个梦想建立无疆帝国的君王、一个征服者。

sentences.en: And I think that's a huge part of what's going on.
sentences.zh: 我认为这正是这些关于亚历山大的故事大行其道的重要原因。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: With these stories about Alexander.
sentences.zh: 关于亚历山大的这些故事。

sentences.en: Didn't Caracola, is it Caracola, the son of Septimius Severus, didn't he, um, model himself on Alexander as well?
sentences.zh: 卡拉卡拉，是塞普蒂米乌斯·塞维鲁的儿子卡拉卡拉吗，难道他不是也把自己塑造成亚历山大那样吗？

sentences.en: And he tried to set up his own phalanx and stuff.
sentences.zh: 他还试图建立自己的方阵什么的。

sentences.en: Isn't that right?
sentences.zh: 难道不是吗？

sentences.en: Well, he invades, he invades Mesopotamia as Alexander had done and is killed while having a pee.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他入侵了美索不达米亚，正如亚历山大曾经做过的那样，结果在小便时被杀。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: He gets off his horse to go to the loo and one of his men kills him.
sentences.zh: 他下马去上厕所，然后他手下的人把他杀了。

sentences.en: That would never have happened to Alexander.
sentences.zh: 这种事绝不会发生在大帝身上。

sentences.en: But they're always doing that.
sentences.zh: 但他们总是这么干。

sentences.en: Crassus does it.
sentences.zh: 克拉苏也这么干过。

sentences.en: Julius Caesar was preparing to do it before he gets assassinated.
sentences.zh: 尤利乌斯·恺撒在遇刺前也正准备这么干。

sentences.en: Mark Antony does it.
sentences.zh: 马克·安东尼也是。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Trajan does it.
sentences.zh: 图拉真也这么干。

sentences.en: Uh, Caracala does it.
sentences.zh: 呃，卡拉卡拉也这么干。

sentences.en: Uh, Julian, the Appostate does it.
sentences.zh: 呃，背教者尤里安也这么干。

sentences.en: They're all invading.
sentences.zh: 他们都在四处征讨。

sentences.en: And it all goes wrong for all of them.
sentences.zh: 结果对他们所有人来说都一团糟。

sentences.en: And it always goes wrong.
sentences.zh: 而且总是以悲剧收场。

sentences.en: And so, and so that again, burnishes the legend of Alexander as someone who could actually do it.
sentences.zh: 所以，所以这再次擦亮了亚历山大作为真正能做到这一点的传奇色彩。

sentences.en: Oh, this absolutely.
sentences.zh: 哦，绝对是这样。

sentences.en: I'm so glad you've said this because this comprehensively proves that I was right when I said Alexander would beat Julius Caesar and Mary Beard refused to answer.
sentences.zh: 我太高兴你这么说了，因为这充分证明了我之前的说法是正确的：亚历山大会打败尤利乌斯·恺撒，而玛丽·比尔德当时拒绝回答。

sentences.en: Uh, when we had her on the podcast talking about classics, we had that crucial question, who would win a fight?
sentences.zh: 呃，当我们在播客中请她来聊古典学时，我们遇到了那个关键的问题：谁能在决斗中获胜？

sentences.en: Lots of people have asked us more of the iterations of this question.
sentences.zh: 很多人向我们询问了这个问题的更多变体。

sentences.en: Who would win a fight?
sentences.zh: 谁能在决斗中获胜？

sentences.en: Genghis Khan, Julius Caesar, Augustus, Napoleon, or Alexander.
sentences.zh: 成吉思汗、尤利乌斯·恺撒、屋大维、拿破仑还是亚历山大。

sentences.en: I mean, I think my answer to that would be that obviously Alexander would win in a fight, but Augustus would win the peace.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我对这个问题的回答是，显然亚历山大会赢得战争，但屋大维会赢得和平。

sentences.en: Do you not think?
sentences.zh: 难道你不这么认为吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, I think so.
sentences.zh: 对，我也这么觉得。

sentences.en: I mean, they seem to me the two poles, actually, of leadership.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在我看来，他们实际上是领导力的两极。

sentences.en: They're the two great figures, the two great paradigmatic leaders of the ancient world.
sentences.zh: 他们是古代世界最伟大的两位人物，也是两位最具范例意义的领导者。

sentences.en: But Alexander's empire doesn't last, and Augustus's does.
sentences.zh: 但亚历山大的帝国没有持续下去，而屋大维的帝国延续了。

sentences.en: And that moment when Octavian, at that point, when he's in the tomb, looking at the body of Alexander, I mean, that's surely one of the extraordinary moments in all history.
sentences.zh: 还有那个时刻——屋大维当时在陵墓里，注视着亚历山大的遗体——我的意思是，这绝对是整个人类历史上最非凡的时刻之一。

sentences.en: Cleopatra has, I think, just died, just killed herself.
sentences.zh: 我想克利奥帕特拉当时刚刚去世，刚刚自杀身亡。

sentences.en: And Octavian goes down, and he goes to see the tomb of Alexander and sort of stares at him.
sentences.zh: 于是屋大维走下去，去看亚历山大的陵墓，默默凝视着他。

sentences.en: And I think he leaves flowers or something.
sentences.zh: 我想他还在那里献了花之类的东西。

sentences.en: And then they say to him, the attendants say, would you like to see the tombs of the Ptolemies now?
sentences.zh: 然后随从对他说，随从问：“您现在想看看托勒密王朝诸王的陵墓吗？”

sentences.en: And he says, no, I didn't come to see a dead man.
sentences.zh: 他说：“不，我不是来看一个死人的。”

sentences.en: I came to see a god.
sentences.zh: “我是来看一个神的。”

sentences.en: I came to see a god.
sentences.zh: “我是来看一个神的。”

sentences.en: And yeah, do you think people will, for hundreds of years, will still talk of Alexander in this sort of ord?
sentences.zh: 是的，你觉得几百年后，人们还会带着这种敬畏谈论亚历山大吗？

sentences.en: Not if they've been listening to you dissing the sources, obviously, but.
sentences.zh: 当然，前提是他们没有听你贬低那些史料。

sentences.en: I think so.
sentences.zh: 我想会的。

sentences.en: And I think the reason for that is in that poem that we began this episode with, the Robert Lowell one, you know, that you can say, yeah, his crimes are terrible.
sentences.zh: 我认为原因就在我们这期节目开篇时读的那首诗里，罗伯特·洛尔的那首，你知道的，你可以说，是的，他的罪行太可怕了。

sentences.en: But they're not crimes, are they?
sentences.zh: 但那其实算不上罪行，对吧？

sentences.en: They're not crimes, even by the standards of the age, they're not even remotely crimes.
sentences.zh: 那根本不是罪行，甚至以那个时代的标准来看，也完全谈不上是罪行。

sentences.en: But what, well, I don't know.
sentences.zh: 但是什么呢，好吧，我不知道。

sentences.en: I mean.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是。

sentences.en: I mean, people at the time didn't say he's a bad man, he's a bad king.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，当时的人们并没有说他是个坏人、是个暴君。

sentences.en: Yes, I think they did.
sentences.zh: 不，我觉得他们说了。

sentences.en: I mean, I think the scale of the slaughter at Tyre.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，泰尔大屠杀的规模……

sentences.en: That's the only instance, though.
sentences.zh: 那只是个例罢了。

sentences.en: Yes, yes.
sentences.zh: 对，对。

sentences.en: But I think the, we live in an un-Alexandrian age.
sentences.zh: 但我觉得，我们生活在一个非亚历山大式的时代。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: People are hostile to the ideal of greatness that he embodies.
sentences.zh: 人们对她所体现的伟大理想抱有敌意。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: People are suspicious of it.
sentences.zh: 人们对此心存怀疑。

sentences.en: But the number of people who replied to this question, I think, indicates that his charisma still blazes bright.
sentences.zh: 但回答这个问题的人数之多，我认为表明他的个人魅力依然光芒万丈。

sentences.en: Absolutely it does.
sentences.zh: 绝对是的。

sentences.en: You know, we are fascinated by apex predators.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们对食物链顶端的掠食者充满着迷。

sentences.en: You know, we're more interested in, tend to be more interested in Siberian tigers or sharks than we are in sheep.
sentences.zh: 你知道，比起绵羊，我们往往对西伯利亚虎或鲨鱼更感兴趣。

sentences.en: Yeah, I'm sure that's true.
sentences.zh: 是的，我确信这是真的。

sentences.en: And I think that Alexander kind of satisfies that need.
sentences.zh: 我想亚历山大在某种程度上满足了这种需求。

sentences.en: On which, no, we should end with.
sentences.zh: 借此，不，我们应该结束了。

sentences.en: Actually, I know how I want to end, Tom.
sentences.zh: 其实，我知道我想怎么结束，汤姆。

sentences.en: No, I want to end with Barry Grogan.
sentences.zh: 不，我想以巴里·格罗根的话来结束。

sentences.en: Well, you can end with Barry.
sentences.zh: 好吧，你可以用巴里的话来结束。

sentences.en: Is that the last question?
sentences.zh: 那是最后一个问题吗？

sentences.en: So Barry, Barry Grogan has said, I'm 31.
sentences.zh: 所以巴里，巴里·格罗根说：我今年31岁。

sentences.en: Can I conquer a similar sized empire by my next birthday?
sentences.zh: 我能在下一个生日之前征服一个同样大小的帝国吗？

sentences.en: I think there's tons of time, Barry.
sentences.zh: 我觉得时间还非常充裕，巴里。

sentences.en: I don't, never give up.
sentences.zh: 我不这么觉得，永远别放弃。

sentences.en: Just don't invade Afghanistan.
sentences.zh: 千万别入侵阿富汗就行。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不。

sentences.en: Well, I mean, you need an oracle.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我的意思是，你需要一个神谕。

sentences.en: Maybe Egypt.
sentences.zh: 也许是埃及。

sentences.en: Maybe Egypt.
sentences.zh: 也许是埃及。

sentences.en: Well, maybe if I read the final lines of my children's history of Alexander the Great.
sentences.zh: 好吧，也许我可以朗读一下我为孩子们写的亚历山大大帝历史书的结尾几行。

sentences.en: That's the way to end.
sentences.zh: 这才是完美的收尾方式。

sentences.en: Then I think that will inspire Barry because this answers his question.
sentences.zh: 然后我觉得这能激励巴里，因为这回答了他的问题。

sentences.en: So I say, it's great that I'm able to quote myself at the end of the podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 所以我想说，我能在播客的结尾引用我自己的话，这太棒了。

sentences.en: Yes, yes, Alexander style modesty.
sentences.zh: 没错，没错，亚历山大式的谦逊。

sentences.en: So here we go.
sentences.zh: 那么我们开始了。

sentences.en: Historians argue about him to this day.
sentences.zh: 历史学家至今仍在争论他。

sentences.en: Some see him as a noble champion of universal brotherhood.
sentences.zh: 有人视他为四海之内皆兄弟的高贵捍卫者。

sentences.en: Others as a selfish monster who cared only for fighting and killing.
sentences.zh: 另一些人则视他为只关心战斗和杀戮的自私恶魔。

sentences.en: How should we remember him?
sentences.zh: 我们该如何铭记他？

sentences.en: Screaming defiance on the field of Gaugamila, slashing decisively through the Gordian knot, bowing his head before the oracle of Ammon or sulking in his tent in the rains of India.
sentences.zh: 是在高加米拉战场上呐喊着反抗、果断斩断戈耳迪之结、在阿蒙神谕前低头，还是在印度的雨中独自在帐篷里生闷气。

sentences.en: All these images are true enough.
sentences.zh: 所有这些形象都足够真实。

sentences.en: But, Tom Holland, perhaps we should remember him as he began.
sentences.zh: 但是，汤姆·霍兰，也许我们应该记住他最初的样子。

sentences.en: As a boy who loved tales of gods and heroes and told his friends that he too would be remembered in poems and songs.
sentences.zh: 作为一个热爱神话和英雄故事的小男孩，他曾告诉朋友们，自己也将在诗歌和歌曲中被后人铭记。

sentences.en: Now, in this at least, and this is a message to Barry, he was not so different from boys and girls everywhere.
sentences.zh: 至少在这点上——这也是给巴里的一个信息——他和世界各地的男孩女孩并没有什么不同。

sentences.en: Did you write that?
sentences.zh: 这是你写的？

sentences.en: Yeah, I'm still going.
sentences.zh: 对，我还没说完呢。

sentences.en: You literally wrote that?
sentences.zh: 这真的是你写的？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Few of us seriously think we are the children of Zeus.
sentences.zh: 我们当中很少有人会认真觉得自己是宙斯的后代。

sentences.en: Few of us.
sentences.zh: 没几个人会这样。

sentences.en: But we all love stories, and we all love to picture ourselves as the heroes of our own adventures.
sentences.zh: 但我们都喜欢故事，我们都喜欢把自己想象成自己冒险故事中的英雄。

sentences.en: And perhaps, inside all of us, there is an inner Alexander.
sentences.zh: 也许，在我们每个人的内心深处，都住着一个亚历山大。

sentences.en: This is a terrifying glimpse into the Sandbrook soul.
sentences.zh: 这是对桑德布鲁克内心世界令人心惊的一瞥。

sentences.en: This is what I tell my son every day.
sentences.zh: 这就是我每天对我儿子说的话。

sentences.en: Perhaps inside all of us, there is an inner Alexander, lifting his eyes to the horizon and dreaming of glory in the world beyond.
sentences.zh: 也许我们每个人的内心深处，都住着一个亚历山大，他将目光投向地平线，梦想着外面的世界的荣耀。

sentences.en: And, well, that's the way to end, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 而且，好吧，这正是完美的结局，不是吗？

sentences.en: I didn't expect that reaction, I have to say, but I'll take it.
sentences.zh: 我必须说，我没想到会有这种反应，但我接受了。

sentences.en: I'll take it.
sentences.zh: 我接受了。

sentences.en: No, it's brilliant.
sentences.zh: 不，这太精彩了。

sentences.en: I haven't yet had the chance to read it, but I can't wait.
sentences.zh: 我还没机会读到它，但我已经迫不及待了。

sentences.en: Clearly, clearly.
sentences.zh: 显而易见，显而易见。

sentences.en: You could do with a laugh.
sentences.zh: 你正需要来点笑声。

sentences.en: I think that may serve to change the entire attitude to Alexander.
sentences.zh: 我想这可能会彻底改变人们对亚历山大的态度。

sentences.en: I think an entire generation may grow up dreaming of becoming Alexander in a way that they used to, back in the good old days of Mary Reynolds.
sentences.zh: 我想整整一代人可能会长大，梦想着成为亚历山大，就像他们在玛丽·雷诺兹的美好旧时代里所做的那样。

sentences.en: Bad news for the people of Iran.
sentences.zh: 这对伊朗人民来说可不是好消息。

sentences.en: Well, no, it may be good news, because they could be integrated into a universal brotherhood of man.
sentences.zh: 噢，不，这可能是个好消息，因为他们可以融入全人类的大兄弟情谊中。

sentences.en: I look forward to it.
sentences.zh: 我对此拭目以待。

sentences.en: So on that happy note, we will see you in a few days for Remembrance Day, a much more solemn occasion.
sentences.zh: 带着这个愉快的心情，我们在几天后的阵亡将士纪念日再见，那是一个更为庄严的时刻。

sentences.en: But we've actually secretly recorded that one firSt.
sentences.zh: 不过其实我们已经偷偷先把那一期录好了。

sentences.en: And you've written a book on that as well, haven't you?
sentences.zh: 而且你关于这个也写过一本书，对吧？

sentences.en: On the First World War, yeah, oddly.
sentences.zh: 关于第一次世界大战的，对，说来也巧。

sentences.en: It's funny how these things happen, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这些事情发生的方式挺逗的，不是吗？

sentences.en: It's weird how they keep propping up.
sentences.zh: 它们总是不断冒出来，真挺诡异的。

sentences.en: Do you have any inspirational messages for boys and girls in that book?
sentences.zh: 你在那本书里有没有给男孩女孩们什么鼓舞人心的寄语？

sentences.en: Yeah, there's a boy and girl inside out, all of us, Tom, beneath the layers of cynicism.
sentences.zh: 有啊，我们每个人内心深处都住着一个男孩和一个女孩，汤姆，在层层玩世不恭的外表之下。

sentences.en: I know the listeners think of me as a much less cynical person than you, clearly.
sentences.zh: 我知道听众们显然觉得我比你没那么愤世嫉俗。

sentences.en: A lovable uncle.
sentences.zh: 一个可亲的叔叔。

sentences.en: Yeah, well, there are different kinds of uncles, aren't there?
sentences.zh: 对，好吧，叔叔也是分好几种的，对吧？

sentences.en: A lovable one.
sentences.zh: 一个可亲的叔叔。

sentences.en: Encouraging boys and girls to invade Persia.
sentences.zh: 鼓励男孩女孩们去入侵波斯。

sentences.en: Right, on that note, see you next time.
sentences.zh: 好啦，那就这样，下次见。

sentences.en: Bye-bye.
sentences.zh: 拜拜。

sentences.en: Bye-bye.
sentences.zh: 拜拜。

sentences.zh: 感谢收听《历史就是这样》。
